principles.title: Ask about sensory needs
principles.text: Lighting, noise, smells and waiting rooms can decide whether an appointment works. Ask before, not after.

principles.title: Make plans visible
principles.text: Share what will happen, in what order, and what will stay the same. Visual schedules help adults as well as children.

principles.title: Allow processing time
principles.text: Pause after questions. Offer written follow-up so information can be revisited.

principles.title: Offer real choices
principles.text: Agree breaks, exits and communication methods, including AAC and written replies.

principles.title: Use clear, literal language
principles.text: Say what you mean. Avoid idioms and vague timeframes such as soon or in a bit.

principles.title: Follow the person's language
principles.text: Many people prefer identity-first terms such as autistic person. Ask and follow their lead.
